problem: T2-FR-01: any retained local outbox row starves unrelated eligible legacy claims in a mixed repository. Static defect, not yet dynamically reproduced.

verdict.reason: A statically demonstrated mixed legacy/local outbox regression requires an actual Astra repair plan, and the original 12-attempt read budget ended with specified quality coverage gaps.

root_cause: protocol._local_target classifies all no-argument outbox claims as local on existence of any local outbox row.
Both dispatch and backend guard run before existing separate legacy store candidate selection.

Memory selection preserves dict insertion iteration and per-candidate _utc_now eligibility; SQLite selection preserves BEGIN IMMEDIATE, existing now, status/next_attempt predicate and ORDER BY id LIMIT 1.
Private operational scope dispatch goes directly to runtime._local_mutate and must remain byte-identical.
Candidate-specific guard under the same storage lock/transaction can preserve local refusal while allowing unrelated unbound legacy delivery.

implementation_contract: For public no-private-scope claim_outbox_message only, defer local target judgment in outer dispatch to actual backend candidate selection under its original storage synchronization. Do not skip checks for any other public writer.

Within memory actual RLock and SQLite actual write lock plus existing BEGIN IMMEDIATE, select the same candidate from the same legacy store with exactly the current iteration/SQL eligibility and order. Check the selected PendingMessage using _local_legacy_write_guard_unlocked with candidate as its argument before mutation. Task binding checks must therefore use current state after waiting for the real lock/transaction.

Adjust _local_target claim-specific global local-outbox-existence fallback to apply only when there is no selected candidate argument. A candidate whose task has a local binding still rejects through existing argument/task checks. An unrelated unbound legacy candidate is not a local target merely because a different local row exists.

When no eligible legacy candidate exists, invoke the original no-argument local guard inside the same actual lock/transaction: retained local outbox implies same scope ValueError and no mutation; otherwise retain None. Do not fall through to reading/claiming local storage.

Do not add a duplicated preflight selection query or time calculation, move check outside synchronization, skip a bound candidate to deliver another, delete local rows, or grant any new scope. Preserve existing private operational branch byte-for-byte.

regression_contract.setup: Use real Memory/SQLite repository instances and real PendingMessage models. Legacy setup uses public enqueue/mark APIs. Local binding/outbox/receipt rows may be explicit test-only persisted-state fixtures under real synchronization; label them descriptive storage fixtures, not live authority or proof of a private run. Include nonempty local receipt data and valid serialized outbox values. No forged private capability or product validator patch.
cases: Pure legacy baseline retains original claim behavior; local-only public claim refuses with original scope error. Freeze before/after full local tasks and publication receipt snapshots, preserving raw value_json/receipt text or memory strings exactly.

Mixed local PENDING row plus unrelated eligible legacy PENDING message: public claim returns exactly legacy id/task with SENDING, updates only expected legacy storage, and all local tasks/receipts remain byte-equivalent. Catch and preserve original ValueError on old source; explicit mixed-legacy-delivery assertion is sole expected RED. Both backend RED runs required.

Repeat a new eligible legacy claim with retained local outbox status SENDING and SENT (test-only state setup under lock, snapshot after setup); local historical status must not globally block. Confirm no double-claim when legacy candidate already SENDING and preserve no-candidate local refusal.

Use existing public legacy failure/backoff path to cover due RETRY_WAIT and future retry suppression without changing product clocks or retry budgets. Verify eligible order remains original when a future-wait legacy row precedes a due message. Local-key mark_outbox_sent/failed continue to refuse with all local snapshots unchanged.

Waited binding recheck: arrange a legacy candidate while task is unbound, start public claimant that waits on actual Memory RLock or actual SQLite independent-connection BEGIN IMMEDIATE. While the real synchronization is held, add binding for that candidate task in the holder, then release/commit. Claim must reject on current binding with no candidate state change and no local modification by claimant. SQLite test uses its real independent connection and original lock/transaction policy, not a fake BEGIN. Record attempted entry, held interval, release and completion.

Test-only delegating lock/connection observation may signal attempted entry but must call the real primitive unchanged. Use Events with bounded waits/joins (5 seconds each), at most one claimant thread per node and two simultaneous SQLite connections. A brief bounded no-completion check while lock held is allowed; no unbounded sleeps, new global profiling, TTL edits or skipped predicate. Finally releases holder/rolls back and joins/closes every actually allocated resource even on RED/failure.

For waited case, take post-binding holder-commit snapshot before claimant proceeds; compare claimant before/after local tasks and receipts byte-for-byte. Also retain original pre-binding snapshot to distinguish authorized fixture preparation from forbidden claimant writes.

Save one case record per node with real source/input hashes, before/after local snapshots, legacy returned record/status, exact exceptions, synchronization phases, thread/connection attempts+closure and registry/no-authority checks. Actual DB files and existing sidecars receive original/archive hashes under existing delivery boundary. No synthetic runtime poll/worker evidence.
